subject: Civil Engineering
title: Tunnel Emergency Egress
description: A micro-lesson that makes Tunnel Emergency Egress usable.

hook.text: In a tunnel emergency, there's no shoulder to pull over and no exit ramp. Egress is designed in.

buildup.text: Emergency recesses — small alcoves with phones and extinguishers — line tunnel walls.

discovery.text: Cross-passages to parallel tunnels or escape galleries provide protected evacuation routes.

twist.text: Pressurized escape galleries keep smoke out — overpressure blows clean air toward evacuees.

climax.text: The Gotthard Base Tunnel has emergency stations every 10 miles with vehicle access for rescue.

punchline.text: The way out is planned before the tunnel is built. Escape is an engineering problem.

quiz.question: How do pressurized escape galleries protect evacuees during a fire?
options: They cool the air to prevent burns during evacuation
Overpressure blows clean air outward, keeping smoke from entering the escape route
They flood with water to extinguish any fire that enters

details.summary: Emergency egress systems in tunnels provide escape routes for people during fires or other emergencies through cross-passages to parallel tunnels, emergency exits to the surface, and emergency walkways along the tunnel length.
details.whyItMatters: Tunnel disasters have shown that egress provisions directly determine survival rates. Modern standards requiring cross-passages every 250-500 meters resulted from lessons learned in fatal tunnel fires.
takeaways: Cross-passages to parallel safe spaces are required every 250-500 meters in road tunnels
Emergency walkways must be wide enough for crowds and wheelchair users
Pressurized safe havens maintain breathable air while occupants await rescue

faq.question: How do cross-passages provide safe escape during a tunnel fire?
faq.answer: Cross-passages connect to a parallel tunnel or dedicated escape corridor maintained at higher air pressure. When the door opens, air flows into the fire tunnel, preventing smoke from entering the escape route. Evacuees walk through the cross-passage into the smoke-free parallel space.

faq.question: What determines the maximum spacing between emergency exits?
faq.answer: Standards require that evacuees reach safety before conditions become untenable. Calculations consider walking speed, crowd density, smoke spread rate, and time to untenable conditions.
